spans.s:
श्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, sharpening, whetting; paring,
&c.
श्यत् श्यत्. See under rt. शो.

स्यात् स्यात्, ind. (properly 3rd sing. Pot.
of rt. 1. अस्), it may be, perhaps, perchance, (स्याद्
अस्ति, it may be, perhaps it is; स्यान् नास्ति, it may
not be.)
—स्याद्-वाद, अस्, m. (probably) assertion
of possibility (in phil.).
—स्याद्वाद-मञ्जरी, f.,
N. of a philosophical work classed under the Ārhata-
darśana in the Sarva-darśana-saṅgraha.
—स्याद्वाद-
वादिन्, ई, m., N. of an Arhat.
—स्याद्-वादिन्, ई, m.
one who asserts possibility.

श्यन् श्यन्, (in grammar) a technical term
for the syllable य or characteristic sign of the fourth
class of roots.
श्यान श्यान, &c. See under rt. श्यै, col. 3.

स्यन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, flowed, trickled, dropped;
dropping, trickling, flowing (as water &c.).

श्यापर्ण श्यापर्ण, आस्, m. pl., N. of a
family; (अस्, आ, अम्), belonging to the Śyāparṇa
family.

श्यापर्णीय, अस्, m. a man belonging to the
Śyāparṇa race.
श्यापर्णेय, see Gaṇa to Pāṇ.

श्याम श्याम, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt.
श्यै or connected with rt. श्वि; cf. श्येत, श्वेत),
black or dark-coloured, dark-blue, dark-brown,
brown; dark-green, green; dark, shady, dusky;
(अस्), m. black, brown, green (the colour); a cloud;
the Kokila or Indian cuckoo; a sacred fig-tree at
Prayāga or Allahabad; a kind of plant (= वृद्-
ध-दारक); epithet of various other trees and
plants (= पीलु; = श्यामाक; = दमनक; = गन्-
ध-तृण); (आस्), m. pl., N. of a Vedic Caraṇa, (a
subdivision^1 of the Maitrāyaṇīyas); the thorn-apple,
Datura Metel; N. of a son of Śūra; (आ), f. night;
shade, shadow; a dark woman; a woman who has
not borne children; another kind of woman (de-
scribed as from eight to sixteen years of age, resem-
bling in complexion the blossom of the Priyaṅgu or
in shape its slender stalk); a form of Durgā (much
worshipped by the Tāntrikas); a cow; a small sing-
ing bird with black plumage (commonly called
Śāmā, Turdus Macrourus); the female of the Indian
cuckoo; a kind of plant (= प्रियङ्गु); turmeric;
the sacred basil; the climbing-plant Ichnocarpus or
Echites Frutescens (= शारिवा); indigo (= नीलिका);
a kind of dark creeper (= कृष्ण-शारिवा); epithet
of various other plants and shrubs (= कृष्णा; =
वागुजी; = गुडूची; = गुग्गुलु; = सोम-लता; =
कृष्ण-त्रिवृता; = गुन्द्रा; = कस्तूरी; = वट-
पत्त्री; = वन्दा; = नील-पुनर्णवा; = नील-
दूर्वा; = पिप्पली; = शिंशपा; = श्यामाक); epi-
thet of the river Yamunā or Jumnā; the seed of
the lotus, = पद्म-वीज; (अम्), n. black pepper;
sea-salt; [cf. Gr. κύανο-ς; Lith. sze†mas; Hib.
ciar, ‘dark-brown, black.’]
—श्याम-कण्ठ, अस्,
m. ‘black-throated, blue-throated,’ a peacock; a
kind of small bird; an epithet of Śiva; [cf. नील-
कण्ठ.]
—श्याम-कन्दा, f. a kind of plant (=
अति-विषा).
—श्याम-कर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, black-
eared; (अस्), m. a horse suitable for a horse-sacrifice.
[]
—श्याम-काण्डा, f. a kind of Dūrvā grass (=
गण्ड-दूर्वा).
—श्याम-ग्रन्थि, इस्, f. = श्याम-
काण्डा.
—श्याम-ता, f. or श्याम-त्व, अम्, n.
blackness, brownness, darkness.
—श्याम-देव, अस्,
m. a proper N.
—श्याम-पत्त्र, अस्, m. ‘black-
leaved,’ the Tamāla tree.
—श्याम-भास्, आस्, आस्,
आस्, of a brilliant black, glossy black.
—श्याम-लता,
f. the climbing-plant Ichnocarpus or Echites Fru-
tescens.
—श्याम-शवल, औ, m. du. Yama's two
watch-dogs, (see शवल.)
—श्याम-सुन्दर, अस्,
m. ‘dark and beautiful,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa.
—श्या-
माङ्ग (˚म-अङ्˚), अस्, ई, अम्, black-bodied, dark-
bodied, black; (अस्), m. the planet Mercury or its
regent.
—श्यामा-पूजा, f. the worship of Śyāmā or
Durgā (on the new moon of the month Kārttika).
—श्यामाम्ली (˚म-अम्˚), f. a kind of shrub (= नी-
लाम्ली).
—श्यामा-रहस्य, अम्, n., N. of a work.
—श्यामी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make black
or dark-coloured.
—श्यामी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति,
&c., to become black or dark-blue.
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210422. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/60.
श्यामाक, अस्, m. = श्यामक above.

श्यामल, अस्, आ, अम्, blackish, black, dark-blue,
brownish, dusky; (अस्), m. black (the colour); black
pepper; the sacred fig-tree; a large bee; (आ), f.,
N. of Durgā or Pārvatī; epithet of various plants
(= अश्व-गन्धा; = कट-भी; = जम्बु; = कस्-
तूरी).
—श्यामल-चूडा, f. a kind of shrub (=
गुञ्जा).
—श्यामलेक्षु (˚ल-इक्˚), उस्, m. a sort of
dark sugar-cane.
श्यामलिका, f. the indigo plant (= नीली).

श्यामाय, Nom. A. श्यामायते, -यितुम्, to be-
come black or dark-blue or green, to prove impure
(as gold).

श्यामायनि, इस्, m., N. of a teacher of the Yajur-
veda.
श्यामायनीय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a Vedic Caraṇa.

श्यामायमान, अस्, आ, अम्, growing dark or
dusk, becoming dusky.

श्यामिका, f. blackness, impurity, alloy (of metals
&c.).
स्यमिक = स्यमीक below.

स्यमीक, अस्, m. a cloud; an ant-hill; a kind of
tree; time; (आ), f. indigo.

श्यामित, अस्, आ, अम्, blackened, turned or be-
come black; darkened, discoloured.

श्याव, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (connected with श्याम),
brown, bay, of a brown or dark-brown colour, dark,
dusky, livid; drawn by bay horses (said of chariots,
Ved.); (अस्), m. brown (the colour); a proper N.;
(आस्), m. pl. the horses of the Sun; (ई), f., Ved.
night (= रात्रि, Naigh.

); [cf. Russ. sivyĭ,
‘dark-grey.’]
—श्याव-तैल, अस्, m. ‘having dark-
brown oil,’ the mango tree.
—श्याव-दत्, अन्, अती,
अत्, or श्याव-दन्त or श्याव-दन्तक, अस्, आ, अम्,
one who has naturally brown or discoloured teeth,
brown-toothed, black-toothed; (according to some
the latter two words may mean ‘having a little tooth
growing between or over the two front teeth.’)
—श्यावाश्व (˚व-अश्˚), अस्, m. ‘having brown or
bay horses,’ N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi, (an Ātreya and
author of several hymns in the fifth, eighth, and
ninth Maṇḍalas of the Ṛg-veda.)
—श्यावाश्वि, इस्,
m. a patronymic of the Vedic Ṛṣi Andhīgu.
श्याव श्याव. See above.

श्याल श्याल, अस्, m. (also written स्याल),
a wife's brother, brother-in-law; a proper N.; (ई),
f. a wife's sister; [cf. Gr. ἀέλιοι, εἰλιόνες.]
—श्याल-
नामन्, आ, &c., called after the name of a brother-
in-law.

स्याल स्याल, अस्, m. (according to Yāska
on Nirukta
VI. 9

. fr. स्य, a winnowing basket, and
ला for लाजा, fried grains, it being the custom for the
bride's brother to scatter fried grains at marriage
ceremonies), the brother of a bride, a wife's brother;
the favourite of a king; a proper N.; (ई), f. a wife's
sister, (also written श्याल); [cf. Gr. ἀέλιοι.]
श्यालिका, f. a wife's sister.

स्य स्य, अम्, n., Ved. a winnowing basket
(= शूर्प, q. v.).

स्या स्या, fem. of the pronoun त्यद् = तद्,
‘he,’ ‘that,’ &c., (nom. c. masc. स्यस्.)
स्यद् स्यद्, स्यद. See below.
स्यद् in रघु-ष्यद्, q. v.

स्यन्द् स्यन्द्, cl. 1. A. (in Fut., Aor., and
Condit. also P., Ved. also P. in other
tenses), स्यन्दते (-ति), सस्यन्दे (
Ved. 3

rd pl.
Perf. P. सिष्यदुस्, Atharva-veda

), स्यन्-
दिषते, स्यन्त्स्यते (स्यन्त्स्यति), अस्यन्दिष्ट,
अस्यन्त (अस्यदत्), स्यन्दितुम्, स्यन्त्तुम् or
स्यन्तुम् (Ved. Inf. स्यन्दयध्यै), to trickle,
ooze, drip, drop, distil, flow, ooze out, flow out; to
flow with, pour forth, shed (with acc.); to run, flee
(P.); (according to Naigh.
II. 14

), to move, rush,
go: Pass. स्यद्यते, Aor. अस्यन्दि: Caus. स्यन्द-
यति, -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. असिस्यन्दत्, -त: Desid.
सिस्यन्दिषते, सिस्यन्त्सते, सिस्यन्त्सति.
स्यद, अस्, m. rapid motion, speed, velocity, rush.
स्यन्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be flowed, &c.

स्यन्त्त्वा or स्यन्त्वा, ind. having flowed; having
rushed on.
स्यान्त्वा, ind. = स्यमित्वा above.

स्यन्द, अस्, m. trickling; going, moving rapidly;
a car, chariot.

स्यन्दत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, moving on, rushing im-
petuously.

स्यन्दन, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, flowing, going quickly;
quick, expeditious, swift; (अस्), m. a war-chariot,
chariot, car; air, wind; the tree Dalbergia Ougei-
nensis (= तिनिश); a particular Arhat of the past era;
(ई), f. saliva; (according to some) the urinary pas-
sage; (अम्), n. the act of trickling, oozing, drop-
ping; rushing, going or flowing swiftly; water.
—स्यन्दन-द्रुम, अस्, m. the tree Dalbergia
Ougeinensis (said to be so called because its wood is
used to make chariot-wheels &c.).
—स्यन्दनारू-
ढ (˚न-आर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, mounted on a chariot or
car.
—स्यन्दनारोह (˚न-आर्˚), अस्, m. a warrior
who fights mounted on a war-chariot.
—स्यन्दना-
लोक-भीत (˚न-आल्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, terrified at the
sight of a chariot.
स्यन्दनि, इस्, m. the tree Dalbergia Ougeinensis.
स्यन्दनिका, f. a drop of saliva.

स्यन्दनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be flowed; to be run;
to be gone.

स्यन्दमान, अस्, आ, अम्, trickling, flowing, mov-
ing rapidly.

स्यन्दितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who runs or rushes
quickly.
स्यन्दित्वा, ind. having flowed; having rushed.

स्यन्द्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. rushing, impetuous; (in
Naigh.
II. 9

. स्यन्द्रासः is enumerated among the
बल-नामानि).

स्यम् स्यम्, cl. 1. P. स्यमति, सस्याम
(3rd pl. सस्यमुस् or स्येमुस्), स्य-
मिष्यति, अस्यमीत्, स्यमितुम्, (according to Vopa-
deva also) cl. 10. P. स्यमयति, &c., to sound, cry
aloud, shout, vociferate; to go, (in Naigh.
II. 14

.
enumerated among the गति-कर्माणः); cl. 10. A.
स्यामयते (sometimes also P. -ति), to consider,
reflect, think: Caus. स्यमयति, -यितुम्, Aor.
असिस्यमत्, to cause to sound: Desid. सिस्यमिषति:
Intens. सेसिम्यते (Pāṇ.
), संस्यन्ति.
स्यमित्वा, ind. having sounded; having gone, &c.
स्यान्त, अस्, आ, अम्, sounded; gone, &c.

स्यमन्तक स्यमन्तक, अस्, m. the jewel
worn by Kṛṣṇa (given to Satrā-jit by the Sun and
transferred by him to his brother Prasena, from
whom it was taken by Jāmbavat, and after much
fighting and contention appropriated by Kṛṣṇa;
the whole story is told in Viṣṇu-Purāṇa
IV. 13

;
the jewel is described as yielding daily eight loads of
gold and preserving from all dangers; it is said to
have been worn by Kṛṣṇa on his wrist, that on
his breast being called Kaustubha).
